'''Jesús Gómez-Gardeñes''' is a Spanish physicist, currently Full Professor (Professor Catedrático) in Condensed Matter Physics at the [[University of Zaragoza]] (Spain).<ref name="unizar_personnel_page">[https://fmc.unizar.es/personal/jesus-gomez-gardenes   Jesus Gómez-Gardeñes profile on University of Zaragoza personnel page]. Retrieved May 17, 2023.</ref> He is known for his works on [[complex systems]], in particular on the structure and dynamics of [[complex networks]].

== Academic career ==

Gomez-Gardeñes received a PhD in physics from the University of Zaragoza in Spain, with a thesis entitled "''Complex Systems: Nonlinearity and Structural Complexity in spatially extended and discrete systems''.” After completing his PhD, he conducted postdoctoral research first at the [[Scuola superiore di Catania|Scuola Superiore di Catania]] (Italy) in the group of [[Vito Latora]], and then in the group of Alex Arenas at the [[Rovira i Virgili University|University Rovira i Virgili]] (Spain). After his postdoctoral period, he joined in 2009 the [[King Juan Carlos University]] in Madrid as Lecturer, before returning in 2011 to his alma mater as a Ramón y Cajal fellow. Between 2019 and 2022 Jesús Gómez-Gardeñes was Associate Professor ([[:es:Titular de universidad|Professor Titular]]), whereas since 2023 he is Full Professor ([[:es:Catedrático de universidad|Professor Catedrático]]) in [[Condensed Matter Physics]]. He leads the Group Of Theoretical and Applied Modeling (GOTHAM lab) at the [[Institute for Biocomputation and Physics of Complex Systems|Institute of Biocomputation and Physics of Complex Systems]].

As of July 2020, he is author of more than 120 scientific articles published in peer-reviewed journals. His [[h-index]] is equal to 51 according to Google Scholar.<ref name="google_scholar">[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=M9cpyEIAAAAJ&hl=en   Jesus Gómez-Gardeñes profile on Google Scholar]. == Research ==

After some initial work in the field of theoretical [[condensed matter physics]], the scientific contributions of Gómez-Gardeñes have focused on the application of [[statistical physics]] methods to the study of [[complex systems]], making him one of the major contributors in the [[network science | network science's]] area of study. Within the latter, he has developed several approaches to investigate the structure and dynamics of networks, in particular to [[multidimensional network]]s. His contributions span a wide range of disciplines ranging from [[mathematical epidemiology]], [[synchronization]], and [[social science]].

Gómez-Gardeñes is well known for his works on the mathematical formulation of multi-scale metapopulation models to integrate human mobility and interaction data on realistic epidemiological frameworks. More specifically, he has studied the spatio-temporal evolution of [[epidemics]], and the evaluation of contention measures.<ref name="brutal_comm_colombia" /><ref name="math_viral" /><ref name="mobility_sci_daily" /> Such a method has been applied to analyze the diffusion of endemic diseases such as the [[Dengue fever]] in Colombia, as well as the diffusion of emergent diseases such as [[COVID-19]] in Spain<ref name="fake_national_geo" /><ref name="article_abc">[https://www.abc.es/ciencia/abci-tres-metodos-matematicos-estan-salvando-vidas-frente-coronavirus-202004062243_noticia.html   ''Los tres métodos matemáticos que están salvando vidas frente al coronavirus.''] ABC (April 7, 2020). Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref><ref name="article_diario_70">[https://www.eldiario.es/castilla-y-leon/cientificos-espanoles-medidas-sanitario-colapsar_1_1010832.html   ''Un grupo de 70 científicos españoles reclama medidas más duras para evitar que el sistema sanitario colapse''.] ElDiario.es (March 22, 2020). Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref><ref name="article_natgeo">[https://www.nationalgeographic.com.es/ciencia/este-mapa-calcula-riesgo-epidemico-coronavirus-hasta-18-marzo_15312   ''Este mapa calcula el riesgo epidémico del coronavirus hasta el 18 de marzo.''] National Geographic Spain (March 23, 2020). Retrieved August 02, 2020.
</ref> and Colombia.<ref name="article_colombia">[https://www.colombia.com/vida-y-estilo/salud-y-bienestar/investigadores-estudian-modelo-matematico-deteccion-covid-19-268423   ''COVID-19: Investigadores estudian nuevo modelo matemático para la detección del virus.''] Colombia.com (April 23, 2020). Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref>

Within the domain of social science, Gómez-Gardeñes is known for his studies on [[evolutionary game theory]] and human [[cooperation]]<ref name="envious_huffpost">[https://www.huffpost.com/entry/envious-personality-types_n_57daff18e4b0071a6e060be8   ''Envious’ May Just Be The Most Common Personality Type.''] Huffington Post (September 15, 2016). Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> and, in particular, for the use of network science tools to analyze human populations, going from large cities<ref name="google_scholar" /><ref name="comm_rich_poor_colombia" /> to small [[hunter-gatherers]] societies.<ref name="article_pais">[https://elpais.com/elpais/2017/08/24/mamas_papas/1503579474_083511.html   ''El juego, clave en los lazos de amistad de los niños.''] El Pais (August 25, 2017). Retrieved August 02, 2020</ref> Finally, he is also known in the field of synchronization theory where he has introduced several approaches to characterize the transition towards dynamical coherence in the [[Kuramoto model]]. In particular, his main achievements include the identification of the mechanism to obtain explosive synchronization transitions in populations of oscillators whose interactions are encoded as a network; and the generalization of the [[Master stability function|Master Stability Function]] to the case of interactions encoded as [[Multidimensional network|multiplex networks]].

== Awards and achievements ==

In 2007, Gómez-Gardeñes was awarded with the ''Investigador Novel'' Prize by the [[Spanish Royal Physics Society]]<ref name="prize_rsef">[https://rsef.es/area-de-miembros/premios-de-la-rsef/item/156-ganadores-del-premio-a-investigadores-noveles   ''Galardonados con el Premio Investigador Novel de la Real Sociedad Española de Física''.] Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> for his works on the structure and dynamics of complex networks.

Gómez-Gardeñes has been visiting researcher at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] in New Mexico (USA), [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (Israel), distinguished visiting professor of the [[National Council for Scientific and Technological Development]] (CNPq) in Brazil, and distinguished visitor of the Scottish Universities Physics Alliance<ref name="supa">[https://www.supa.ac.uk/   Scottish Universities Physics Alliance]. Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> (SUPA). In 2019, Gómez-Gardeñes was appointed as Fellow of the Institute for Computational Social Science<ref name="kobe_ccss">[http://ccss.kobe-u.ac.jp/en/index.html#:~:text=Center%20for%20Computational%20Social%20Science%20(CCSS)%20of%20Kobe%20University%20promotes,computational%20science%20and%20data%20science   Center for Computational Social Science Kobe University]. Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> of the [[University of Kobe]] (Japan).

He is chair and founder of the Latin American Conference of Complex Networks<ref name="lanet_conf">[http://www.lanetconference.org/   LANET conference homepage]. Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> (LANET), an international conference aimed at spurring the field of network science in the Latin American community. Moreover, he serves since 2013 as associated editor of the ''[[Journal of Complex Networks]]'' (Oxford University Press),<ref name="jconn_edboard">[https://academic.oup.com/comnet/pages/Editorial_Board   Journal of Complex Networks -- Editorial board]. Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> and also as a member of the editorial board of Journal of Physics: Complexity,<ref name="jopcom_edboard">[https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/2632-072X/page/Editorial_board   Journal of Physics: Complexity -- Editorial board]. Retrieved August 02, 2020.</ref> a scientific journal published by the Institute of Physics.
